tour.text:
Two loops from Perth, with a rest-day reset in the city in between. The south loop follows the coastal classics to Esperance and, depending on your nerve, on to Cape Arid or Israelite Bay — the way back is not the same road, but through the Goldfields (ghost towns, the Lake Ballard sculptures).

The north loop comes in three levels: from the relaxed coastal classic via the peninsula expedition (Steep Point, Dirk Hartog, Quobba — the recommendation) to the outback expedition through the Gascoyne to Karijini and into the East Pilbara to the “Eel Pool” from the insider notes.

Every place below carries labels (must-see / hidden gem / 4WD only / expedition), every route has a map preview and a link to the real Google Maps view.

kalender.text: Vehicle pick-up, big shop, final check of park pass & bookings (Shelter Bay, Temple Gorge, Dirk Hartog barge).
Margaret River to Esperance/Cape Arid incl. Yeagarup Dunes & Stokes NP — with 2 more days of breathing space than the 12-day core (e.g. beach/buffer days in Esperance).

kalender.titel: Return as a Goldfields loop (or direct in 2 days)
kalender.text: Esperance → Kalgoorlie → Lake Ballard → Gwalia → Perth. Alternatively direct via Wave Rock (2 days, 1 more buffer day).
Vehicle check, laundry, supplies for the north — or a Rottnest day (book the ferry!).
Recommendation: North 2 “Peninsula expedition” (17–20 days, 3–6 buffer days). North 3 only for fully self-sufficient crews (fills the whole window).
Vehicle return/cleaning, reserve for weather delays, flight home.

praxisWarnung: <div class="box-title">⚠ The three hard rules for Dec/Jan
praxisListe: Book ahead (some months ahead): Shelter Bay/Steep Point (DBCA Park Stay), Dirk Hartog barge (from Blackies Beach, max. 20 vehicles on the island), Temple Gorge/Kennedy Range (booking required since April 2026), Maggies Camp/Warroora — and for the islands: Rottnest ferry (January = school holidays!), Woody Island boat/huts, Abrolhos flight tour.
Permits: Rio Tinto rail road Tom Price → Millstream: free 30-day permit (online or Tom Price Visitor Centre). Otherwise no special permits needed on the northern routes.
Park pass: 4-week Holiday Pass $70 covers both loops — buy in advance at shop.dbca.wa.gov.au.
Fuel in the north: Gascoyne Junction, Mount Augustus Tourist Park and Tom Price are the only sources in the hinterland — plan for 600+ km range. Gnaraloo only sells fuel with 24 hours' notice.
Tyres: deep sand (Steep Point, Peron, Gnaraloo, Yardie): let down to 16–20 psi; compressor at Peron Homestead, otherwise bring your own.
Bushfires in the south: no open fires/barbecues on total fire ban days; check EmergencyWA daily.
Gwalia museum: closed on some days over Christmas and the turn of the year — call ahead then.
